findings.why: The commit does contain the test it claims (bootstrap_repo with a credentialed URL, asserting [REDACTED] and no leak), redact_secret itself has its own unit tests in src/utils.rs, and the production code is conceded correct, so asking for stronger assertions and for the other five redaction sites to be exercised is a coverage request on tested, correct code.

UPSERT_PATCHSET_SECTION_SQL does overwrite source unconditionally (confirmed, same as the bug-side UPSERT_BUG_SUBSYSTEM_SQL), but a demotion needs the same string to arrive once as a MAINTAINERS title and once as a path prefix or caller string, and no ingestion caller exists at this commit (path-prefix names are directories, section names are titles), so the defect cannot be confirmed.

replace_patchset_maintainer_sections does run its SELECT, DELETEs and upserts as autocommit statements with no transaction while update_bug_subsystems wraps the bug-side twin, but the method has no caller yet and a backfill can wrap it with the pub begin_transaction/commit_transaction, so whether the non-atomicity is a defect depends on code not in the commit.

Confirmed that the merge transaction copies patchsets_subsystems but not patchset_maintainer_sections before DELETE FROM patchsets, and the new table cascades with foreign_keys ON; whether rows are lost depends on an ingestion caller that writes sections to a row before it is merged, which does not exist at this commit.

The compressor does BEGIN IMMEDIATE on the single shared Database.conn and awaits inside the window, so another task's autocommit write would join that transaction; but this is a pre-existing property of every writer, the ROLLBACK path needs a per-row compressor error to coincide, and the new writers have no caller, so the loss cannot be confirmed.

No upstream rule requires audit triggers on this table, there is no patchset audit sink to write to, the finding itself calls the gap hygiene with nothing reading the rows, so this is a design suggestion rather than a defect.

Same claim as A0: the unconditional DO UPDATE SET source = excluded.source is confirmed, but a same-name/different-source collision through the non-existent ingestion caller is not shown, so the demotion is a hazard that cannot be confirmed as a defect.

Same claim as A1: the pub replace method is non-transactional where the bug-side wrapper is transactional, but with no caller and pub transaction helpers available the atomicity defect cannot be confirmed either way.

Admits the code under test is not necessarily wrong; the new methods have five tests, so asking for a downgrade case, a cascade case and a CHECK-constraint case is a request for more coverage on tested code.

Same claim as A2: the merge routine omits the new table and the cascade is enforced, but loss only occurs once an ingestion caller attaches sections to a row that is later merged, which is not in this commit.

Same claim as A4: missing audit triggers is a mirroring/design suggestion with no upstream rule behind it and nothing reading the rows; the finding concedes the migration comment's mirror claim is accurate for columns and constraint.

Speculates about a transcript gate and a backfill that do not exist in this commit; an empty table after a migration is the documented meaning of authorizes-nobody, the index remarks are preferences, and the COLLATE NOCASE point concerns a query nobody has written.

Same claim as A0/B0: overwrite-on-conflict is confirmed, the BTreeMap last-wins in replace is confirmed, but a realistic same-name/different-source input through a caller that does not exist cannot be confirmed.
Same claim as A1/B1: non-transactional replace confirmed, defect status depends on the absent backfill caller.
The finding itself concedes the upserts are idempotent, add is a union, a retry converges and the failure is closed, so no defect with a consequence is claimed.
Same claim as A4/B4: absence of audit triggers is a design suggestion, no upstream rule requires them, no patchset audit sink exists, and nothing reads the rows.

The commit message states the server bypass and non-interactive intent, --agent taking precedence over --format and --interactive is the designed behaviour, and asking for conflicts_with or help text is a UX preference with no defect.

Admits this is regression risk not a present defect; the commit tests the new logic (formatter, clap parsing, skip_report worker run), so asking for tests of the remaining plumbing branches is a coverage request on correct code.

Confirmed that run_worker_in_worktree returns review:null for --no-ai and the formatter maps it to clean while the text path prints No AI review was run; but the only public trigger is the explicit --no-ai flag, documented as only testing that patches apply, for which clean is a defensible answer, so the defect cannot be confirmed.

status reports whether findings exist and the pre-existing exit code encodes the gating policy (new High/Critical); nothing upstream says the two must agree, each finding carries severity and preexisting, and result_has_error requiring a non-empty string is not shown to be reachable with an empty error.

A hard failure before any result exists still gives a non-zero exit and stderr diagnostics, empty stdout distinguishes it from a findings exit 1, the exit-code scheme is pre-existing, and the commit message only promises error metadata inside the JSON of a produced result.
The server bypass is the stated purpose of the flag, the missing wall-clock timeout on wait_with_output is pre-existing for every local run and is a hardening preference, not a confirmed defect.

Same claim as A4: failures before a result exist exit non-zero with stderr output and empty stdout, which is a conventional and distinguishable CLI failure, and the commit message does not promise JSON for pre-result failures.
Same claim as A0: the overrides are the designed, commit-message-stated behaviour of --agent; missing conflicts_with or help text is a preference.
Skipping the dirty-worktree prompt is the stated purpose of the flag, the stderr warning remains, and a dirty field in the JSON is a feature request with no defect.

The new feature has tests (formatter, parsing, worker skip_report run) and the untested guard in review_single_patch is correct, so asking for tests on additional branches is a coverage request on tested, correct code.

Same claim as A2: review:null maps to clean, confirmed, but the public trigger is explicit --no-ai where clean (patches applied) is defensible and the empty-range trigger is unverified, so not confirmable as a defect.
Same claim as A3: status and exit code answer different questions, the exit policy is inherited, per-finding severity and preexisting are present, and no upstream document requires agreement.

Same claim as A4/B0: pre-result failures exit non-zero with stderr and empty stdout, which is distinguishable from a findings exit; the exit-code collision is pre-existing and the commit message does not promise JSON for them.

Same claim as A2/B4: confirmed mapping of review:null to clean, but the realistic trigger is the explicit --no-ai flag whose documented purpose is only checking patches apply, so a defect cannot be confirmed.
Same as A0/B1 plus docs: the overrides and prompt bypass are intended, no upstream rule requires docs/sashiko-cli.md to list every flag, and a dirty field is a feature request.
Concedes the worker test is not vacuous and that the failure would be cosmetic; the retain filter is correct and the feature is tested, so this is a request for one more test on correct code.
Worker discovery by file existence is pre-existing and applies to any new flag; a stale worker fails loudly with a clap error, and a version handshake is a design suggestion.

Confirmed that the log level is chosen from the variant before the retry-exhaustion check, so the terminal NotIndexedYet give-up is logged only at info while the row is marked Failed with the reason in error_log; whether a terminal give-up must be logged at error is an operational policy not stated upstream, so the defect cannot be confirmed.

The arithmetic is confirmed (max_retries 3, backoffs 5s and 30s, 180s tier unreachable), but whether ~35s is shorter than Patchwork's mirror lag is unknown and the finding admits it, so incompleteness of the fix cannot be confirmed either way.

Restates A1 (35s window, then Failed) plus A0's log level; same confirmed mechanism, same unverifiable premise about mirror lag, and a permanent empty list ending as a recorded Failed row is bounded and honest.

Same claim as A0: info-level log on the terminal NotIndexedYet attempt is confirmed, but the row is correctly marked Failed with the reason stored, so it is an observability policy question rather than a confirmed defect.
Same claim as A1: the ~35s shared budget is confirmed, the sufficiency against real Patchwork indexing lag is not determinable from the code.
Same claim as A0/B0: terminal NotIndexedYet attempt logged at info while marked Failed, confirmed mechanism, unconfirmed as a defect since the state and stored reason are correct.
Same claim as A1/B1: retry window arithmetic confirmed, adequacy against external mirror lag unverifiable.

Same log-level mechanism as C0 with an unverified misconfiguration premise; an HTTP 200 with [] is inherently indistinguishable from lag, the row ends as a recorded Failed, and the suggested error_log wording is a preference.
